items.title: Localising twice is the localisation at the image of the first multiplicative subset
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for multiplicative subsets S and S' of a ring A, the localisation at the product set is isomorphic to the localisation of the localisation at S' at the image of S (statement lines 1492-1496). Unlike the module version of the same phenomenon, the proof does not construct the two maps on fractions: it obtains each of them by applying the universal property of the localisation twice, first to the composite map from A and then again because the relevant elements become invertible, and checks that the two are inverse by the same mechanism (proof lines 1498-1513). Recognising that the universal property is available here, where for modules it is not yet established, is what determines the shape of the argument. H2.
